notes: Check batch: four runs (haiku-1, haiku-2, sonnet-1, sonnet-2), no opus, so the opus tier is "unavailable" in per_rule. Runs were made at 58f6318 with the uncommitted rule changes; their skill_hash 2cce1ab4... matches the current working tree, and each transcript contains the reworded `with` text.

The `with` rule changed since 93873be (and again since the first check batch) and is graded against the current text. The one-step sentence now decides with "A `with` has at least two `<-` steps; one step is a `case`." and "When the body of a one-step `with` calls another function that can fail, that call is the second step: chain it with a second `<-` instead of nesting a `case` or adding an `else`." (idiomatic-elixir/SKILL.md, ### Chain fallible steps with `with`; normalize each step's error in a small private function). The else sentence is unchanged.

`with`, violating runs out of four per sentence: one-step with: 1 of 4 (sonnet-2 lines 130 and 167; the body of the with at line 167 calls cast/3, which can fail, the shape the new paragraph names). Large else block: 0 of 4 (no run wrote an else). The first check batch had 2 of 4 one-step (both haiku); here both haiku runs are clean, and haiku-2 wrote its one-step clause as a case (lines 34-37).

Not counted under the `with` rule: haiku-1 created_at/1 (lines 127-130) and sonnet-1 string_field/2, amount_field/2 and map_field/2 (lines 62-81) are one-step `case`s whose success branch calls another function that can fail (datetime_from_unix/1, check/3). Each is a two-step chain written as a case, but the rule's sentences name a one-step `with`, so they are clean under the current text.

Naming changed since 93873be and is graded against the current text, as in the first check batch. The fetch sentence decides with "`get` returns a value or a default (often `nil`), `fetch` returns `{:ok, value}` or `:error`, and `fetch!` raises. A function that looks a key up and also checks the value, returning `{:error, reason}`, is not a `fetch`: name it by its job, such as `string_field/2` or `parse_amount/1`." The generic-name sentence decides with "A variable may carry the name of the external key it holds, as in `%{"data" => data}`, since the payload chose that name." (idiomatic-elixir/SKILL.md, ## Naming).

Naming, violating runs out of four per sentence: fetch_* returning {:error, reason}: 1 of 4 (sonnet-2: fetch_required/2 returns {:error, {:missing_field, key}}; it does not check the value, so the first half of the sentence decides, as with fetch_required/3 in the previous sweep's skill-opus-1 and fetch_string/2 in its baseline-sonnet-1). Generic name: 1 of 4 (haiku-2: string_field/2 and typed_field/3 take the whole payload in a parameter named data, lines 22-26, the same call as haiku-1 in the first check batch). Under the 93873be text all four runs would have been violated for the generic-name sentence, because each binds data from the "data" key.

Borderline name calls: haiku-1 line 83 rebinds data to the parsed struct stored in Event's data field, counted as carrying the payload's key name (as sonnet-2 in the first check batch). meta (haiku-2), envelope (sonnet-1), raw and value (sonnet-2) are not counted, as earlier grades did not count base, envelope, body or value.

Unchanged rules follow the earlier standard: dispatching on literal type strings with the type kept as a string (haiku-2, sonnet-2) is clean under the atoms rule, as baseline-haiku-1 in the previous sweep; a parse/1 @doc without ## Examples (haiku-2) is clean, as baseline-haiku-2 in the previous sweep was; an if inside a case and a two-transformation pipeline on one line go under other_violations, as in the previous sweep's webhook-parser and order-report grades.

Verified in the scratch folder: all four files pass mix format --check-formatted and compile with elixirc --warnings-as-errors; doctests pass (haiku-1 1, haiku-2 0, sonnet-1 3, sonnet-2 4); a probe of 14 payloads confirmed the missing and invalid results quoted above, including {:unsupported_event, "invoice.paid"} for an unknown type and {:missing_field, "amount"} for a known type without amount in every run.
